newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX seen consolidating under 2,750 level.
newsitem.headline: German DAX seen consolidating under 2,750 level.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares was expected to consolidate in the coming week after reaching new record highs, although dealers said the DAX could try to edge up somewhat towards 2,750 points.

"The market in general could try slowly but surely inch up higher. Most people now are turning positive on Germany, even some of the old bears," said one dealer. "But we might need some sideways consolidation first."
The IBIS DAX, which measures all-day computer trade in the DAX, was up 6.96 points at 2,724.46 in late dealings, off day-highs after Wall Street opened weaker.
Dealers said the publication of the price range for soon to be floated Deutsche Telekom shares would be a focus on Monday.
The reporting of blue-chip companies SAP AG and RWE on Tuesday will also be closely watched.
SAP gained over one percent on Friday to trade up three marks in computer dealings at 282 marks and traders said good results were expected from the firm.
German M3 money supply, due out early next week, is expected to have grown at an seasonally adjusted annualised rate between 8.2 and 8.5 for September.
"Beyond the M3, all that remains is the good old U.S.," said one dealer, "But even there not much is expected. We'll probably just be reacting to little bits of corporate news."
On Friday, sportsware firm Adidas was one of the main losers, down four marks at 138 in late IBIS on rumours of earnings downgrades by various banks.

At the other end of the spectrum, Fresenius Medical Care added over eight percent in computer trade, up 10.25 marks at 135 marks. The bourse newcomer has attracted a lot of interest since its launch at the start of October.
